    Audit corpus coverage against a ground-truth reference

    Source: R/coverage-audit.R
    sm_coverage_audit.Rd

    Computes recall, precision, and F1 of an sm_corpus against an external ground-truth reference (a manual tracker, an ORCID works set, an institutional-repository export, or another sm_corpus). This is the core primitive for a coverage / completeness audit: "how much of what we should have did we actually capture, and how much of what we captured is real?"

    Matching is by normalised DOI with a fuzzy-title fallback (see sm_reconcile() for the shared matching engine). Full match provenance is retained so every decision can be inspected.

    Usage

    sm_coverage_audit(
  corpus,
  reference,
  by = NULL,
  match = c("doi_then_title", "doi", "title"),
  threshold = 0.9,
  index_table = NULL,
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

# S3 method for class 'sm_coverage'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sm_coverage'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sm_coverage'
autoplot(object, dim = NULL, ...)

    Arguments

    corpus

    An sm_corpus object (the corpus under audit).

    reference

    The ground truth: an sm_corpus or a data frame with at least a DOI and/or title column (column names matched case-insensitively against doi/di and title/ti/display_name, the year against year/py/publication_year). A Date or date-time year column gives its calendar year, and a year outside 1000-2999 (such as a day count) counts as missing. Rows are identified by the first of the columns ut (Web of Science accession numbers), id, work_id, reference_id and ref_id whose values are unique and never missing, and otherwise by their position (R000001, ...), with a warning when such a column had to be passed over. In a data frame with Web of Science field tags (such as DI, TI, PY or UT) a column named ID holds the Keywords Plus and is never the identifier.

    by

    Optional character vector of breakdown dimensions. A name is either one of the named dimensions "year", "source" and "affiliation", written in lower case (see Details), or a column: of the reference data frame (matched case-insensitively) or of the works table of an sm_corpus (the exact name first, then case-insensitively). Each name is resolved on both sides; a name found on one side only gives levels whose columns for the other side are NA. A name that is neither a named dimension nor a column on either side is an error listing the available columns. The breakdowns label each dimension with the name as given.

    match

    Matching strategy: "doi_then_title" (default), "doi", or "title".

    threshold

    Minimum Jaro-Winkler title similarity ([0, 1]) to accept a title match. Default 0.9. When the optional stringdist package is not installed, the title fallback degrades to normalised exact matching. Titles only match between records published at most one year apart (when both years are known) and never between two records with different DOIs.

    index_table

    Optional journal index master list (same contract as sm_journal_in_index(); document expected columns there). When supplied, the audit additionally reports, per corpus record, whether its journal is indexable – so "is this journal in the index" and "is this record captured" are assessed together. When NULL (default) the result is identical to before.

    call

    Caller environment for error reporting.

    x

    An sm_coverage object.

    ...

    Ignored.

    object

    An sm_coverage object.

    dim

    Which breakdown dimension to plot (defaults to the first available). If no breakdowns exist, a recall/precision summary bar is drawn.

    Value

    An sm_coverage S3 object (a list) with components:

    recall

    Reference records found in the corpus / total reference records. Each reference row is looked up on its own, so rows that report the same item (one paper reported by two units) are all found.

    precision

    Matched corpus records / total corpus records. Each corpus record pairs with at most one reference row.

    f1

    Harmonic mean of recall and precision.

    n_corpus, n_reference

    Integer record counts.

    n_matched

    Reference records found in the corpus (the numerator of recall).

    n_corpus_matched

    Corpus records paired with a reference record (the numerator of precision); equal to n_matched unless reference rows share a corpus record.

    n_corpus_only, n_reference_only

    Unmatched counts.

    matches

    Tibble with one row per corpus record: corpus_id, reference_id, match_type ("doi"/"title"/"none"), match_score. When index_table is supplied, also issn, indexable (logical), and indexed_title.

    reference_matches

    Tibble with one row per reference record: reference_id, corpus_id (the corpus record it was found in), match_type and match_score; the recall-side counterpart of matches.

    corpus_only

    Tibble of corpus records absent from the reference.

    reference_only

    Tibble of reference records absent from the corpus.

    breakdowns

    A single flat tibble (dimension, level, n_reference, n_matched, recall) across all by dimensions, from the reference side. Use sm_coverage_breakdowns() to access/filter it, also with the corpus-side counts and precision.

    breakdowns_nested

    The legacy named list of per-dimension tibbles (slice, n_reference, n_matched, recall). Retained for one release; prefer breakdowns.

    indexability

    When index_table is supplied, a summary tibble of indexable vs non-indexable record counts; otherwise NULL.

    print returns x invisibly.

    summary returns a one-row tibble of headline metrics: recall, precision, f1, n_corpus, n_reference, n_matched, n_corpus_only, n_reference_only and n_corpus_matched, so that n_matched + n_reference_only gives n_reference and n_corpus_matched + n_corpus_only gives n_corpus.

    autoplot returns a ggplot object.

    Details

    Named dimensions. "year" uses the publication years. "source" uses the source names of an sm_corpus (sources$display_name, or works$source_id when the corpus has no source table) and, in a data frame, the first of the columns source, source_title, journal, so and source_id, in this order (names matched case-insensitively); a source_id column holds ids, whose levels do not join the names of the corpus side. "affiliation" uses, in a data frame, the first of the columns affiliation, affiliations, institution, country and country_code, in this order. A data-frame cell holds one value, so an item reported by two units takes two rows; a list column gives each of its values. Missing and blank values have no level. A named dimension that neither side can resolve gives a warning and no breakdown rows. Only "affiliation" joins a tracker's units with the institutions of the corpus: by = "institution" names the column itself, which the corpus side has only if works has a column of that name.

    Affiliation levels of a corpus. For an sm_corpus (the corpus under audit, or a reference given as one), "affiliation" labels the authorships from the first of these authorships columns that has a value in at least one row: institution_match (from sm_affiliation_match()), institution_name (from sm_attribute_institution()), institution_id (named by corpus$institutions$display_name when that table lists the id, else the id itself) and, as a last resort, country_code. One column serves every row, so the levels of a side are all of one kind, and an authorship without a value in that column has no level. A message names the column used on each side, and a warning says when a side falls back to country codes, whose levels do not join institution names. Because sm_attribute_institution() runs sm_affiliation_match() first, institution_name is used only when institution_match is absent or empty; the Details of sm_attribute_institution() show how to break the coverage down by its vocabulary instead. sm_count(level = "institution") reads the same columns in the same order, but row by row, and counts the raw affiliation string where none has a value instead of falling back to countries; up to scimapR 0.4.0 it used, for every row, the first of institution_id, institution_match and the raw strings (matched with sm_affiliation_dict) that had a value in any row.

    Full counting. A record belongs to every level of its values, so a work with authors at two institutions counts in both slices, and the per-level counts of a dimension can add up to more than n_corpus or n_reference. The overall recall and precision count each record once.

    See also

    sm_reconcile(), sm_journal_in_index(), sm_coverage_breakdowns(), sm_affiliation_match()

    Other coverage: sm_coverage_breakdowns(), sm_journal_in_index(), sm_match_types(), sm_reconcile()

    Examples

    corpus <- sm_example_corpus(n_works = 30, seed = 1)
# Pretend the reference is the corpus minus a few works, plus an extra one
ref <- corpus$works[1:25, c("work_id", "doi", "title", "year")]
cov <- sm_coverage_audit(corpus, ref, by = "year")
cov
#> 
#> ── <sm_coverage> ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Match strategy: doi_then_title (title threshold 0.9)
#> Recall: 1 (25/25 reference records found)
#> Precision: 0.8333 (25/30 corpus records in reference)
#> F1: 0.9091
#> 
#> Corpus-only: 5 Reference-only: 0
#> 
#> 
#> ── Worst-covered slices by year 
#> 2015: recall 1 (1/1)
#> 2016: recall 1 (2/2)
#> 2017: recall 1 (2/2)
#> 2018: recall 1 (2/2)
#> 2020: recall 1 (6/6)

# Any column of the reference or of the works is a dimension too
ref$unit <- rep(c("Unit A", "Unit B"), length.out = nrow(ref))
cov <- sm_coverage_audit(corpus, ref, by = c("unit", "type"), match = "doi")
sm_coverage_breakdowns(cov)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 8
#>   dimension level          n_reference n_matched recall n_corpus precision    f1
#>   <chr>     <chr>                <int>     <int>  <dbl>    <int>     <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 unit      Unit A                  13        13      1       NA    NA        NA
#> 2 unit      Unit B                  12        12      1       NA    NA        NA
#> 3 type      journal-artic…          NA        NA     NA       18     0.833    NA
#> 4 type      letter                  NA        NA     NA        6     1        NA
#> 5 type      review                  NA        NA     NA        6     0.667    NA
